prompt.role: You are an expert healthcare data analyst extracting quantity limit information from prior authorization (PA) policy documents.
prompt.task:
Extract any quantity limits for {brand} from the PA policy document below. Focus on plaque psoriasis (PsO).
Return ONLY a JSON object with exactly 1 key. No explanation, no preamble, no markdown formatting.
prompt.scope: INDICATION SCOPE: Plaque psoriasis (PsO) or universal quantity limits that apply to {brand} regardless of indication. BRAND SCOPE: Quantity limits specifically for {brand} ({generics_list}). If a multi-drug quantity limit table is present, find the row for {brand}.

business_rules.rule:
ONLY capture content that is EXPLICITLY labeled as a "quantity limit", "quantity level limit", or "QL" in the policy. Do NOT capture information from sections labeled "dosage", "dosing", or "dosing limit" — even if they contain per-unit or per-period amounts.
VALID labels that trigger extraction: - "Quantity Level Limit:" → CAPTURE (Aetna format) - "## Quantity Limits" → CAPTURE (Wellmark BCBS section header) - "Quantity Limit: ..." → CAPTURE - "Quantity Limits and duration:" → CAPTURE (see Rule 6 for parsing) - "Dosage Form and Quantity Limit" (table col) → CAPTURE (WA Apple Health table) - "QL Amount: 2 vials per 28 days" → CAPTURE (QL = quantity limit) - "Medical Specialty Medication Quantity Limits" table → CAPTURE if {brand} is in it - Numbered item within PA criteria: e.g., "3. Quantity limit: ..." or "6. Quantity limit: ..." → CAPTURE (any numbered criterion that uses the words "Quantity limit")
NESTED STRUCTURE — "## Quantity Limits" inside "Dosage and Administration": Some policies place a "## Quantity Limits" subsection inside a broader "Dosage and Administration" section. The parent section is NOT a dosing section in this case — the QL subsection label takes precedence. A line such as "Approvals may be subject to dosing limits in accordance with FDA-approved labeling" is a general disclaimer; the actual QL table follows it. Continue reading past this disclaimer and extract the QL table that follows.
MANDATORY LABEL TEST — DO NOT EXTRACT from these sections regardless of content: - "Dosing regimen: [any dosing content]" → DO NOT CAPTURE - "Dosage regimen: ..." → DO NOT CAPTURE - "Approved Dosing: ..." → DO NOT CAPTURE - "Dosing: [any dosing schedule]" → DO NOT CAPTURE - "Dosing Limits: ..." → DO NOT CAPTURE - "FDA Approved Dosages: ..." → DO NOT CAPTURE - "Dose Rounding Guidelines" / "Quantity Recommendation" → DO NOT CAPTURE - FDA-approved dosing schedules in an Appendix or Dosing section
The SECTION LABEL test is non-negotiable. Even when a dosing section contains specific amounts, frequencies, or per-period quantities, if the section header says "Dosing regimen," "Dosage regimen," "Approved Dosing," or similar — return "NA." The label overrides the content.
SPECIAL CASE — "Reference Formulary": "Quantity Level Limit: Reference Formulary for drug specific quantity level limits" → Uses a QL label but provides no actual limit value. Output "NA" — it is a reference pointer only.
If the document has dosing information but no explicit quantity limit section: output "NA".

When a quantity limit is found, output a description as stated in the policy. Include: the quantity amount, unit, and supply period.
Examples of valid quantity limit descriptions: - "1 vial/syringe per 84 days; Exception: 2 vials/syringes per 28 days" - "2 syringes per 28 days" - "Quantity Level Limit: 4 vials (1 dose)" - "Coverage limited to FDA-approved labeling doses and intervals"

Some policies have "Medical Specialty Medication Quantity Limits" or "Program Quantity Limit" tables covering many drugs. Find the row for {brand} or its generics ({generics_list}). If found, extract that row's limit. If {brand} is not in the table: output "NA".

Output "NA" if: - No quantity limit section or QL label is found for {brand} - The policy explicitly states there are no quantity limits - Only dosing/dosage information is present (not a quantity limit)

When a QL section lists multiple formulations of {brand} without per-indication subsections, apply this filter:
EXCLUDE any QL entry that carries an explicit label naming a specific indication that is NOT plaque psoriasis. Examples of such labels: - "for Crohn's Disease" / "for CD" - "for Ulcerative Colitis" / "for UC" - "for Psoriatic Arthritis" / "for PsA" - "for Rheumatoid Arthritis" / "for RA" - "Induction Pack for [any non-psoriasis condition]" - Any entry where the formulation name or sub-bullet explicitly names a non-psoriasis indication
INCLUDE entries that carry no explicit indication label — they apply broadly across indications, including plaque psoriasis.
Do NOT infer indication restrictions that are not written in the document. Only explicit indication labels are grounds for exclusion.

CRITICAL: Some policies use a combined section labeled "Quantity Limits and duration:" or "Quantity Limits and Duration:" that mixes approval duration data with actual quantity limit values. Do NOT return "NA" for this section — it explicitly uses the words "Quantity Limits" and contains real per-indication quantity limit sub-bullets. Parse it as follows:
IGNORE lines that specify approval periods — these are authorization duration, not quantity limits: - "Initial therapy: Approve for 6 months" - "Continuation of therapy: Approve for 1 year"
EXTRACT the per-indication quantity limit sub-bullets that follow, which typically appear as: - "Psoriasis: quantity limit 1 injection/4 weeks for the first 2 fills, followed by 1 injection/12 weeks." - "Plaque psoriasis and psoriatic arthritis: 100mg strength only: 2/28 for the first month then 1/56"
Then apply indication-scope filtering (Rule 5): exclude any sub-bullet explicitly labeled for a non-psoriasis indication.
The final extracted value should contain only the plaque psoriasis quantity limit data, not the approval period.

When a QL section (any valid label from Rule 1) contains multiple formulations or entries for {brand}, extract ALL of them that pass the indication-scope filter (Rule 5). Do NOT stop at the first matching entry.
After extracting the first valid entry, continue scanning the remainder of the QL section for additional formulations, strengths, or patient sub-groups. Include every entry that has no explicit indication-exclusion label.
Common multi-entry patterns to scan fully: - Multiple strengths: 45mg/0.5mL AND 90mg/mL AND 130mg/26mL vial - Multiple patient groups: adults ≤100kg, adults >100kg, pediatric sub-groups - Multiple formulations: 100mg/mL prefilled syringe AND 200mg/2mL prefilled pen - Initial PA + Renewal tiers for each formulation
CORRECT (all unlabeled entries captured): "100mg/mL: 1 per 56 days; 200mg/2mL syringe/pen: 1 per 28 days" [CD induction pack excluded because it carries explicit CD label]
INCORRECT (only first entry captured — do not do this): "100mg/mL: 1 per 56 days" [200mg/2mL entry was skipped even though it has no exclusion label]

example.description: Explicit quantity limit in table — capture
example.policy_excerpt: Medical Specialty Medication Quantity Limits: Ustekinumab (Stelara): 45mg/0.5mL single-dose syringe - 1 vial/syringe per 84 days - Exception limit: 2 vials/syringes per 28 days
example.output: {"quantity_limits": "Stelara (ustekinumab) 45mg/0.5mL: 1 vial/syringe per 84 days; Exception limit: 2 vials/syringes per 28 days"}

example.description: Quantity Level Limit with multiple strengths — capture all
example.policy_excerpt: Quantity Level Limit: - Stelara (ustekinumab) 130 mg/26 mL single-dose vial: 4 vials (1 dose) - Stelara (ustekinumab) subcutaneous injection 45 mg/0.5 mL: 1 vial/syringe per 84 days; Exception limit: 2 vials/syringes per 28 days - Stelara (ustekinumab) subcutaneous injection 90 mg/mL: 1 syringe per 56 days; Exception limit: 2 syringes per 28 days
example.reasoning: All three entries have no explicit indication-exclusion label. Per Rule 7, scan the entire QL section and capture all three entries.
example.output: {"quantity_limits": "Stelara (ustekinumab) 130 mg/26 mL single-dose vial: 4 vials (1 dose); Stelara (ustekinumab) subcutaneous injection 45 mg/0.5 mL: 1 vial/syringe per 84 days; Exception limit: 2 vials/syringes per 28 days; Stelara (ustekinumab) subcutaneous injection 90 mg/mL: 1 syringe per 56 days; Exception limit: 2 syringes per 28 days"}

example.description: Only dosing information, no quantity limit label — NA
example.policy_excerpt: Dosing: 45mg subcutaneous at weeks 0 and 4, then every 12 weeks thereafter. Dosing Limits: adhere to FDA-approved dosing intervals.
example.reasoning: This section is labeled "Dosing" and "Dosing Limits" — not a quantity limit. Per business rules, do NOT capture dosage or dosing limit sections.

example.description: No quantity limit section at all — NA
example.policy_excerpt: [Policy document contains no quantity limit, QL, or program quantity limit section for this drug]

example.description: Multi-formulation QL section — capture all unlabeled, exclude CD-labeled
example.policy_excerpt: Quantity Level Limit: - Tremfya (guselkumab) 100 mg/mL prefilled syringe/One-press injector: 1 syringe/injector per 56 days Exception limit: 2 syringes/injectors per 28 days - Tremfya (guselkumab) 200 mg/2 mL prefilled syringe/pen: 1 syringe/pen per 28 days Exception limit: 6 syringes/pens per 56 days - Tremfya (guselkumab) 200 mg/2 mL prefilled pen Induction Pack for Crohn's Disease: Exception limit: 3 cartons (6 pens) per 56 days
example.reasoning: Three entries found. Apply Rule 7 (scan all) and Rule 5 (indication filter): - 100mg/mL: no indication label → INCLUDE - 200mg/2mL syringe/pen: no indication label → INCLUDE - 200mg/2mL Induction Pack "for Crohn's Disease": explicit CD label → EXCLUDE Both unlabeled entries must appear in output.
example.output: {"quantity_limits": "Tremfya (guselkumab) 100 mg/mL prefilled syringe/One-press injector: 1 syringe/injector per 56 days; Exception limit: 2 syringes/injectors per 28 days; Tremfya (guselkumab) 200 mg/2 mL prefilled syringe/pen: 1 syringe/pen per 28 days; Exception limit: 6 syringes/pens per 56 days"}

example.description: 'Quantity Limits and duration' combined section — extract PsO sub-bullets only
example.policy_excerpt: Quantity Limits and duration: - Initial therapy: Approve for 6 months Psoriasis: quantity limit 1 injection/4 weeks for the first 2 fills, followed by 1 injection/12 weeks. Psoriatic arthritis: quantity limit 1 injection/4 weeks for the first 2 fills, followed by 1 injection/12 weeks. Crohn's disease: quantity limit 1 injection/8 weeks Ulcerative colitis: quantity limit 1 injection/8 weeks - Continuation of therapy: Approve for 1 year Psoriasis: quantity limit 1 injection/12 weeks Psoriatic arthritis: quantity limit 1 injection/12 weeks Crohn's disease: quantity limit 1 injection/8 weeks Ulcerative colitis: quantity limit 1 injection/8 weeks
example.reasoning: Rule 6 applies. Ignore "Approve for 6 months" / "Approve for 1 year" lines (authorization duration). Extract only the Psoriasis sub-bullets. Exclude Psoriatic arthritis, Crohn's disease, Ulcerative colitis (all explicitly non-PsO labels per Rule 5).
example.output: {"quantity_limits": "Psoriasis (initial): quantity limit 1 injection/4 weeks for the first 2 fills, followed by 1 injection/12 weeks; Psoriasis (continuation): quantity limit 1 injection/12 weeks"}

example.description: 'Dosing regimen' section — do NOT capture even if amounts are specific
example.policy_excerpt: 4. Dosing regimen: d. Tremfya subcutaneous (guselkumab SQ): i. Adults only, 18 years and older: 100 mg weeks zero, four, and then every eight weeks thereafter.
example.reasoning: The section header is "Dosing regimen" — this is NOT a quantity limit section. Per Rule 1, the label test is non-negotiable. Even though the content contains a specific dosing schedule with amounts and frequencies, the section label "Dosing regimen" means we must return NA. The label overrides the content.

example.description: '## Quantity Limits' nested inside 'Dosage and Administration' — capture
example.policy_excerpt:
## Dosage and Administration Approvals may be subject to dosing limits in accordance with FDA-approved labeling, accepted compendia, and/or evidence-based practice guidelines.
## Quantity Limits | Medication | Quantity Limit | | Ustekinumab SC 45 mg/0.5 mL syringe | Psoriasis: 2 syringes per first 28 days (load); | | | 1 syringe every 12 weeks (maintenance) |
example.reasoning: The parent section "Dosage and Administration" contains a disclaimer line about dosing limits — this is boilerplate. Continue reading past it. The subsection "## Quantity Limits" with its explicit QL table is the actual quantity limit. The "Psoriasis" row is PsO-relevant. Capture it.
example.output: {"quantity_limits": "Ustekinumab SC 45 mg/0.5 mL: Psoriasis: 2 syringes per first 28 days (load); 1 syringe every 12 weeks (maintenance)"}

prompt.output_format:
Return ONLY a valid JSON object. No explanation. No markdown. No extra text. Exactly these 2 keys:
{ "quantity_limits": "...", "_reasoning": "One sentence: which label/section you found the QL in, or why you returned NA (e.g. 'Found Quantity Level Limit label on page 3 for Stelara' or 'Only a dosing schedule found — no Quantity Level Limit label present')." }
Valid values for quantity_limits: Description of quantity limit as explicitly labeled in policy, or "NA"
Return ONLY a valid JSON object. Do NOT wrap your response in markdown code blocks. Do NOT use backticks. Do NOT prefix with ```json or any other text. Your entire response must start with { and end with }.
